explanation: A dense 'Latin-script, English-like running text' dial: from the second token on it sits at about 0.25-0.6 of max on almost any English sentence, and it also crosses 0.25 on ALL-CAPS English sentences, English-ish code, SQL, HTML, URLs, e-mail addresses, key-value and signature lines and comma-separated number lists. It peaks (>0.7 of max) on a quantifier, particle or preposition right after a frequency/polarity adverb or verb ('never any', 'never once', 'always some', 'ever come across', 'had any'). It is ~0 on all non-English language text (French, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, lorem ipsum, Cyrillic, CJK) and on English words that follow a non-English opening (only a 'never any' pair climbs back to ~0.4-0.7). It is also ~0 on the same word repeated, on ordered runs (years, weekdays, AAAA BBBB), on random-letter, base64 or hex strings, on bare keyword or name runs such as 'import os import sys' and on two-word greetings or labels ('Hi there', 'Best regards', 'Sales Department').
